advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Remove the unused `--no-refresh` flag or wire it to actual behavior (and reconcile the README/docstring wording).
evidence: ap.add_argument("--no-refresh", action="store_true", help="(report) read the committed ledger; do not record")
search for `no_refresh` in the module returned no matches — the attribute is never consumed
report() at line 326-332 unconditionally reads the ledger and never records; there is no --report-side record path to suppress
advisory.finding: The `--no-refresh` CLI flag is declared but its argparse attribute `args.no_refresh` is never read; `report()` never auto-records under any condition, so the flag is a no-op that contradicts the README/docstring framing of it as controlling record-vs-read behavior.
advisory.suggested_fix: Drop the `--no-refresh` argument since `--report` already never records, or make `--report` optionally record unless `--no-refresh` is set.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Change the incremental watermark comparison to `<` and rely on the existing dedup key for idempotency at the boundary.
evidence: watermark = max((int(r["ts"]) for r in existing), default=-1)
if not backfill and ts_ns <= watermark: continue
dedup via `seen`/`_dedup_key` only runs on rows produced by files that pass the watermark filter, so files skipped by `<=` are never deduplicated in
advisory.finding: Incremental `--record` skips any sidecar whose `ts_ns` equals the current watermark (`ts_ns <= watermark`), so a newly-added review sharing the exact max recorded timestamp is never read and the dedup guard (which only applies to rows that were read) cannot recover it.
advisory.suggested_fix: Use `if not backfill and ts_ns < watermark: continue` and let `_dedup_key`/`seen` handle the equal-ts boundary idempotently.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure the ticket's true latest review round (even one with only indeterminate/abstained findings) is reflected when computing latest_ts/latest_verdict_pass, or document the abstain-only-latest-round assumption.
evidence: for f in payload.get("findings") or []: if f.get("decision") == "indeterminate": continue  (line 106 — such rounds emit no rows)
round_ts = sorted({int(r["ts"]) for r in trows}); latest_ts = round_ts[-1] (line 185-186 — computed only from emitted rows)
is_remediated = is_resolvable and (not info["in_latest"]) and latest_verdict_pass (line 218 — keyed off the possibly-not-actually-latest round)
advisory.finding: `latest_ts` and `latest_verdict_pass` are derived only from recorded rows; a review round whose findings are all `indeterminate` yields zero rows and thus never appears in `round_ts`, so if the true latest round was all-abstain the detection logic treats an earlier round as 'latest' and may mislabel a still-open fix-unit as remediated.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a compute_effectiveness fixture where a fix-unit is `dropped` in the SAME round it first blocks (and one where the only drop precedes any block) and assert it does NOT count as de-escalated.
evidence: harness: `de_escalated = any(dts > first_blk for dts in info["drop_ts"])`
test_blocking_fp_proxy_counts_gate_de_escalation only uses drop at ts=2 after block at ts=1 (test_criterion_effectiveness.py:155-158)
ABSENCE: no fixture has a `dropped` firing at the SAME ts as (or before) the first `block` firing, so the `> first_blk` boundary is unverified
advisory.finding: The de-escalation temporal guard `de_escalated = any(dts > first_blk for dts in info['drop_ts'])` (the documented 'dropped in a round AFTER its first blocking appearance' rule) is never exercised at its boundary: every FP-proxy fixture drops the fix-unit strictly after the blocking round, so a regression that relaxes the guard (e.g. `>`→`>=`, or counting a drop at/before the first block) would still pass. blocking_fp_proxy is the metric the promotion gate reads, so this is regression-blindness on load-bearing logic.
scenarios: A refactor changes the drop-after-block comparison and silently inflates/deflates blocking_fp_proxy, misdirecting the advisory→blocking promotion decision
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test with rows `_row('T',1,'block',['X'],'u1')` and `_row('T',1,'dropped',['X'],'u1')` (same ts) asserting `blocking_fp_proxy == 0.0`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a compute_effectiveness fixture with a fix-unit blocking under criteria `['A','B']` and assert both A and B record the blocking fix-unit / detection / FP.
evidence: harness: `if r["d"] == "block": info["blk_crits"].update(r["c"])`
every compute_effectiveness fixture uses a single-criterion firing, e.g. `_row('T1',1,'block',['X'],'u1')` (test_criterion_effectiveness.py:135)
ABSENCE: no fixture blocks one fix-unit under 2+ criteria to assert both criteria receive the detection/FP attribution
advisory.finding: Multi-criterion blocking attribution is untested. `info['blk_crits'].update(r['c'])` attributes a blocking fix-unit to every criterion it cites and the metric sets key on `(ticket, fix_unit)`, but no fixture has a single fix-unit blocking under two or more criteria — yet the committed corpus has multi-criterion ids (e.g. G1G2) and findings citing `['G6','E4']`. The per-criterion fan-out that produces the committed numbers is unverified.
scenarios: A regression in the blk_crits fan-out under-/over-counts blocking_fix_units for co-cited criteria, skewing per-criterion detection_proxy

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a firings_from_review case with a finding carrying `drop_reason='novelty'` and assert the resulting row's `x == 'novelty'`.
evidence: harness: `"x": f.get("drop_reason")`
test asserts `"x": None` only (test_criterion_effectiveness.py:105)
ABSENCE: no finding fixture with `drop_reason` in {'novelty','completion'} asserting it flows to row `x`
advisory.finding: The `x` (drop_reason) firing-row field is never asserted with a non-null value. firings_from_review captures `"x": f.get("drop_reason")` and the ledger schema documents floor labeling (FLOOR_DROP_REASONS), but the only extraction test asserts `x: None`, so a regression that drops or mislabels drop_reason capture would pass.
scenarios: drop_reason capture is broken/renamed; the future floor-era segmentation the schema promises is silently lost

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a record() test over a tmp tracker dir (injected fingerprint fns) asserting a second run adds 0 rows (idempotent) and that a sub-watermark sidecar is skipped in incremental mode but seen under --backfill.
evidence: harness watermark filter: `if not backfill and ts_ns <= watermark: continue` (line 307)
harness dedup: `key = _dedup_key(row); if key not in seen:` (line 317-319)
test docstring: 'The live-store --record path is exercised out-of-band (the AC proving commands)' (test_criterion_effectiveness.py:8-9)
ABSENCE: no test drives record() over a temp tracker dir with monkeypatched fingerprint fns to assert idempotency/watermark/schema-filter
advisory.finding: The `record()` I/O seam is entirely untested: idempotency (dedup-key skip), the incremental watermark filter `ts_ns <= watermark`, the USABLE_SCHEMAS guard, and the malformed-JSON skip have no test — the change defers them to out-of-band commands. These have concrete plausible regressions (e.g. `<=` vs `<` at the watermark, a dedup key that omits round_uuid) that no committed test would catch.
scenarios: A watermark off-by-one re-appends or skips firings; a dedup-key change duplicates rows into the append-only ledger

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the documented `--no-refresh` behavior with the implementation (either wire the flag or remove it from docstring/README/argparse help since `--report` never records).
evidence: README example: `... --report --no-refresh  # writes runs/criterion_effectiveness.json (reads the committed ledger; never auto-records)`
argparse help: `ap.add_argument("--no-refresh", action="store_true", help="(report) read the committed ledger; do not record")`
In main(): `if args.report:\n        metrics = report(window=args.window)` — `args.no_refresh` is never consulted; `report()` never records regardless
dropped.finding: The `--no-refresh` flag is documented (in the module docstring, the experiments README, and argparse help) as controlling whether `--report` records, but the flag is never read in `main()`—`--report` always calls `report()` which only reads the committed ledger. The documented distinction between `--report` and `--report --no-refresh` does not exist, so the docs describe a no-op behavior.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] State the `--window` default (400) in the module docstring's WHAT IT DOES section to match the README and argparse help.
evidence: docstring: `--report [--window N]   Compute per-criterion effectiveness over the trailing window` (no default stated)
README: `default 400`
code: `DEFAULT_WINDOW = 400`
dropped.finding: The module docstring's WHAT IT DOES / usage examples omit `--window` for `--report` but the README and plan-review-gate.md prominently document a default window of 400; the docstring's `--report [--window N]` line does not state the default, creating an inconsistency in where the default 400 is discoverable versus the code's `DEFAULT_WINDOW = 400`.
